_comment: How Swordfish's client names become clients in Raptor. Held as data, not code, because
these are business judgements that were made in conversation and will be revisited — a
reviewer should be able to check them without reading an importer.
Swordfish conflates three different things in one 'Client' field: the client, the
sub-entity, and the handover batch. Growthpoint appears four times and is one client with
four handovers; Adowa appears twice and is one parent with two properties that each keep
their own book. Importing the field as-is would produce eleven unrelated clients and no
Superseded by the client report once that is supplied — this exists so the account import
is not blocked waiting for it.
Superseded in part by the Jan 2026 client list: that file is authoritative for the
commission rate, BF reference, owner, banking and contact details, joined on Prefix.
What stays here is the grouping judgement the client list cannot express — that four
Growthpoint records are one client, and that Adowa's two properties are children of one
parent. Swordfish's rates are per record because that is how it fakes a sliding scale.

clients.name: Adowa Property Managers (Pty) Ltd
clients._note: Parent only. Two properties, each with its own account book, so they are children rather than sequential handovers of one relationship.

children.name: Adowa Property Managers — Ellis Park
swordfish: Adowa Property Managers (Pty) Ltd - Ellis Park

clients.name: Growthpoint Student Accommodation Holdings (RF) Ltd
clients._note: One client, four handovers. Swordfish splits it across two client codes (GPS3/GPS4) and files them under different groups (Rentals/Schools), but it is one relationship — and one sliding-scale commission agreement, which only works if the client is one record.
